items.title: Chezmod
items.text: Helpers for managing a chezmoi dotfiles repo with gum-driven prompts. Covers apply, diff preview, add or forget flows, and update or re-add actions.

items.title: Functions
items.text:
• chd: Open the chezmoi source directory in yazi.
  • chad: Add files to chezmoi with optional interactive selection.
  • chfo: Forget managed files from chezmoi with optional selection.
  • chra: Check upstream freshness, preview reverse diff, sync the host-specific Hypr monitor template when available, and run chezmoi re-add.
  • chup: Preview pending diff and run chezmoi update after confirmation.

items.title: Aliases
items.text:
• ch: Run chezmoi.
  • chap: Confirm and run chezmoi apply.
  • chdiff: Show reverse diff (excluding scripts) through delta.

items.title: Cross-machine re-add safety
items.text:
chra checks the Git repository at chezmoi source-path, fetching the current branch's configured upstream remote before comparing commits. It does not assume a remote or branch name, and never pulls, merges, or applies dotfiles automatically.

If the branch is behind or diverged, chra warns and defaults to cancellation. The same confirmation is required when freshness cannot be verified, such as when offline, without Git or an upstream, on a detached HEAD, or using a non-Git source. You can explicitly continue anyway, then review the usual diff. Unresolved merge conflicts stop the operation without an override. Ahead-only branches and ordinary staged, unstaged, or untracked changes remain allowed.

Re-add copies this machine's files back into the source repository. Git being up-to-date does not prove newer source changes have been applied locally; the diff cannot distinguish intentional edits from stale machine state. Review and reconcile source and machine changes before proceeding. All confirmations default to No; declining or unavailable confirmation prevents both the monitor-template copy and chezmoi re-add. Fetching may still update Git's remote-tracking metadata.

items.title: Tests
items.text: Run npm test to exercise the guard with temporary local Git repositories and mocked interactive commands. Tests do not access real dotfiles or the network.
